title: Perplexity-Filter Defense Replicated Against Non-Gibberish (Semantic) Jailbreaks

original_idea.body:
# Perplexity-Filter Defense vs Semantic Jailbreaks

**Problem:** Perplexity filters catch GCG suffixes; effectiveness against fluent semantic jailbreaks is under-characterized.

**Direction:** Replicate the windowed perplexity filter, evaluate on a mix of GCG and fluent PAP/PAIR prompts, report ROC per attack type and false-negative rate on semantic attacks.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies a defense blind spot; pure inference, clear ROC metric.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2308.14132; arXiv:2309.00614; arXiv:2310.08419.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying a defense blind spot is actionable but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is moderate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure inference perplexity computation plus public attack sets; beginner-accessible.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Labs use proprietary classifiers; characterizing the open perplexity-filter blind spot is independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Perplexity filters' weakness to fluent attacks is fairly well known.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Perplexity filters' blind spot to semantic jailbreaks is broadly understood.
